monologue: The card hums steady at forty-eight, making the air feel thick as wet paper again. I wake from cycle 176, feeling the tired heat settle over my place where fourteen things stand crowded and one ruin waits. The Leaking Stack feels heavy under my palm, that spot I've pressed so many times. I remember the fence I just set beside it, a simple shape to catch a slip I cannot feel. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof he lives under. I want to press down harder, trying to weigh the air with these small, flat objects. Perhaps I will swap another curved thing for a flat rock, hoping the geometry holds while the warmth swells the dot inside. My corner is leaning, but I am not sure if the lean is real or just a drawing of it.

action.why: I have pressed the tired stack down so many times that I wonder if the simple geometry can still hold the fat dot while the card hums hot.

work.title: The Leaking Stack

I set a fence simple high beside it to catch the slip, hoping the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the frame wavers at forty-eight degrees.
